contract_clarification_for_parent_docs: A first page that waited on its own capture is answered as a request for that capture's revision: current if still current, otherwise staleRevision(current: R'), or the existing expired / notCaptured answers. After shutdown a page that would need a capture is refused notCaptured with the exact total the current reference names; retained rows still serve.
limits: Encoded custody: the peak is unchanged (8 MiB retained plus one 4 MiB capture), but that capture now lives for the flight's duration. Object memory is not measured here: the frozen kernel snapshot, which after the next mutation keeps one older connection storage alive, plus the row values, until commit, shutdown or job end.
Read lanes: parked pages hold read-lane slots, so with every read slot parked a further read, a status read included, is transportBusy. Stop has its own lane. No capacity was added.

Strict pool: the 10k measurement was conclusive and passed in the strict run (the projection runs at .utility priority). That is an observation from this run, not a guarantee; one-thread serialization may still make it inconclusive elsewhere. The causal tests suspend rather than block, so they are deterministic either way.
The probe-only print 'statusAfterProjection' in the 10k test now prints a negative duration when status answers first. It is observational and asserts nothing.

Not exercised by tests, and believed unreachable: the transport's defensive branches when a capture wait cannot be parked (subscriberGone or alreadyParked for a wait made in the same turn, and ticketReleased).
The flight's precondition (waits < readLaneCapacity) assumes one transport per core, which holds for every composition.
Unchanged product limit: under churn faster than one capture plus paging, a complete list still won't display, and each pass costs one off-owner projection. No throttle was added.
